name: Bramble-Char
description: Bramble-Char is a small, tortured moon-world caught in a tidal lock with its gas giant parent, its interior squeezed and heated by gravitational forces that keep its core partially exposed along a massive equatorial rift. From orbit, the rift glows like a wound, and the branching lava channels that spread from it across the surface resemble the thorned stems of some burning bush, giving the world its name. An orbital debris ring of ejected volcanic material encircles the planet in a thin, glittering band.

The low gravity means that volcanic ejecta reaches extraordinary altitudes, and the sky above Bramble-Char is a constant rain of cooling rock fragments that patter against the surface in a sound like hail on metal. The toxic atmosphere is thin enough that stars are visible through the volcanic haze, their light dimmed and reddened by the particulates. The exposed core pulses with a rhythmic glow that follows the tidal cycle, brightening as the gas giant reaches closest approach.

Bramble-Char has no history of habitation and no particular mystery. It is simply a world in the process of being torn apart by forces it cannot resist, its geology laid bare for any passing ship to observe. Survey records note it primarily as a navigational hazard, its debris ring extending further than initial scans suggest and its volcanic eruptions occasionally reaching altitudes that threaten low orbit.

Despite its hostility, Bramble-Char's exposed core offers a rare opportunity to study planetary interior composition without the expense of deep drilling. Remote sensing from orbit has revealed iron and copper concentrations that would be valuable if they were accessible, but the combination of constant eruption, tidal instability, and corrosive atmosphere makes surface operations impractical. Bramble-Char exists as a geological curiosity, beautiful in its destruction, useful only to those who study the mechanics of dying worlds.
